The seal receipt

You will learn

What receipt an agent reads before it reuses a spec, and in which order the verdict is decided.

An agent about to reuse a spec asks for the receipt of its seal, and seal_verdict answers with one of 7 words in a fixed order: unsealed when there is no seal of this spec, unknown when the seal cannot be compared, stale when the source changed after the seal, forced, failing, vacuous when no sealed test asserts anything, and verified. The seal file name is the parent folder and the module, so two specs can derive one name, and a seal that records another path is no seal of this one. Here fresh means only that the spec bytes are the sealed bytes: t27c seal --verify is the full check.

Try it

Take the good seal and change one digit of the current source. Then force it past a failure, and then give it a test that asserts nothing.

Open the interactive lesson →

Before an agent reuses a spec it asks for the seal receipt. Seven verdicts, decided in order, from unsealed to verified. Set the facts of a seal and read its receipt.

specs/t27mcp/seal_verdict.t27

// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
; specs/t27mcp/seal_verdict.t27 -- the seal receipt of t27_spec in the t27 MCP server (gHashTag/t27-mcp): what a
; spec's seal says about the spec an agent is about to reuse. See #10066 (epic), the validated-code contract:
; t27_find and t27_spec hand out code, this hands out the receipt for it.
; --
; The rules are not written here. specs/verified/seal_check.t27 decides what a seal's parts mean (fail closed:
; a part that cannot be compared is UNKNOWN, a forced seal is never a pass, a seal that failed a test is a
; failure) and specs/verified/reuse.t27 owns the PART_* codes. This file calls seal_check_alg() and maps its
; answer onto the words an agent reads. It adds three things the checker does not have:
; - the seal belongs to the asked spec: the seal file name is <parent dir>_<module>.json, so two specs can
;   derive one name (gHashTag/t27#8540). A seal whose recorded spec_path is another path is no seal of this one.
; - the digest comparison: the server hashes the current source, this compares the two "sha256:<hex>" strings
;   byte for byte. A string that is not that shape is not an observed part.
; - vacuous: a green seal with no test, or with a test that asserts nothing, verifies nothing.
; The seal records the hashes of the four generated backends too. The server cannot regenerate them, so they are
; passed as PART_SAME: "fresh" here means the spec bytes are the sealed bytes, nothing more. `t27c seal --verify`
; is the full check.
; --
; Verdicts, in the order they are decided: unsealed, unknown, stale, forced, failing, vacuous, verified.
; phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY

module T27mcpSealVerdict;

use verified::reuse;
use verified::seal_check;

/// seal_verdict() answers; the index into VERDICT_NAME and VERDICT_NOTE.
pub const SV_UNSEALED : u32 = 1;
pub const SV_UNKNOWN : u32 = 2;
pub const SV_STALE : u32 = 3;
pub const SV_FORCED : u32 = 4;
pub const SV_FAILING : u32 = 5;
pub const SV_VACUOUS : u32 = 6;
pub const SV_VERIFIED : u32 = 7;

pub const VERDICT_NAME : [8]str = [
    "none", "unsealed", "unknown", "stale", "forced", "failing", "vacuous", "verified"
];

pub const VERDICT_NOTE : [8]str = [
    "",
    "No seal of this spec: nobody has run its tests into a receipt. Run t27c test-report before you rely on it.",
    "The seal cannot be compared with the source (no or unknown digest). Treat as unverified.",
    "The source changed after the seal. The seal says nothing about this text; reseal it before you rely on it.",
    "The seal was forced past failing tests. It is not a pass.",
    "The sealed run had failing tests.",
    "The seal holds no test that asserts anything, so it verifies nothing.",
    "The source is the sealed source and its sealed tests passed."
];

/// The length of a string.
pub fn str_len(s: string) -> u32 {
    return (s.len as u32);
}

/// 1 when a and b are the same bytes, 0 otherwise.
pub fn same_bytes(a: string, b: string) -> u32 {
    var n : u32 = str_len(a);
    if (n != str_len(b)) { return 0; }
    var i : u32 = 0;
    while (i < n) {
        if ((a[i] as u32) != (b[i] as u32)) { return 0; }
        i = i + 1;
    }
    return 1;
}

/// ALG_SHA256 when h is "sha256:" and 64 more characters, 0 for any other shape.
pub fn hash_alg(h: string) -> u8 {
    if (str_len(h) != 71) { return 0; }
    var pre : string = "sha256:";
    var i : u32 = 0;
    while (i < 7) {
        if ((h[i] as u32) != (pre[i] as u32)) { return 0; }
        i = i + 1;
    }
    return ALG_SHA256;
}

/// The spec part of the seal: MISSING when either digest is not a sha256 string, else SAME or DIFF.
pub fn spec_part(recorded: string, current: string) -> u8 {
    if (hash_alg(recorded) != ALG_SHA256) { return PART_MISSING; }
    if (hash_alg(current) != ALG_SHA256) { return PART_MISSING; }
    if (same_bytes(recorded, current) == 1) { return PART_SAME; }
    return PART_DIFF;
}

/// 1 when the source the server hashed is the source the seal recorded.
pub fn is_fresh(recorded: string, current: string) -> u32 {
    if (spec_part(recorded, current) == PART_SAME) { return 1; }
    return 0;
}

/// The verdict on one seal. has_seal is 0 when no seal file was found. The test counts come from the seal's
/// tests object; an absent vacuous count is 0, an absent tests object is total 0.
pub fn seal_verdict(has_seal: u32, seal_path: string, path: string, recorded: string, current: string, total: u32, passed: u32, failed: u32, failing_n: u32, vacuous: u32, forced: u32) -> u32 {
    if (has_seal == 0) { return SV_UNSEALED; }
    if (same_bytes(seal_path, path) == 0) { return SV_UNSEALED; }
    var green : bool = false;
    if (failed + failing_n == 0) {
        if (passed == total) { green = true; }
    }
    var c : u8 = seal_check_alg(hash_alg(recorded), spec_part(recorded, current), PART_SAME, PART_SAME, PART_SAME, PART_SAME, green, forced != 0);
    if (c == CHECK_SPEC_DIFF) { return SV_STALE; }
    if (c == CHECK_FORCED) { return SV_FORCED; }
    if (c == CHECK_FAILED) { return SV_FAILING; }
    if (verdict_pass(c) == false) { return SV_UNKNOWN; }
    if (total == 0) { return SV_VACUOUS; }
    if (vacuous > 0) { return SV_VACUOUS; }
    return SV_VERIFIED;
}

pub const H_A : string = "sha256:66cc87ba315b75ba80b51b6813d84cb238149e6e75a4f1f55a5fec4915be7c1f";
pub const H_B : string = "sha256:66cc87ba315b75ba80b51b6813d84cb238149e6e75a4f1f55a5fec4915be7c1e";

test "a seal of this spec, the same bytes, passing tests is verified" {
    assert seal_verdict(1, "specs/a/x.t27", "specs/a/x.t27", H_A, H_A, 3, 3, 0, 0, 0, 0) == SV_VERIFIED;
    assert is_fresh(H_A, H_A) == 1;
}

test "no seal file is unsealed" {
    assert seal_verdict(0, "", "specs/a/x.t27", "", H_A, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0) == SV_UNSEALED;
}

test "case twin: a seal recorded for another path is not a seal of this spec" {
    assert seal_verdict(1, "specs/b/x.t27", "specs/a/x.t27", H_A, H_A, 3, 3, 0, 0, 0, 0) == SV_UNSEALED;
    assert seal_verdict(1, "specs/a/X.t27", "specs/a/x.t27", H_A, H_A, 3, 3, 0, 0, 0, 0) == SV_UNSEALED;
    assert seal_verdict(1, "", "specs/a/x.t27", H_A, H_A, 3, 3, 0, 0, 0, 0) == SV_UNSEALED;
}

test "negative control: one changed digit makes the seal stale, not fresh" {
    assert seal_verdict(1, "specs/a/x.t27", "specs/a/x.t27", H_A, H_B, 3, 3, 0, 0, 0, 0) == SV_STALE;
    assert is_fresh(H_A, H_B) == 0;
    assert seal_verdict(1, "specs/a/x.t27", "specs/a/x.t27", H_A, H_B, 3, 1, 2, 2, 0, 1) == SV_STALE;
}

test "fail closed: a digest that is not sha256 is unknown, never fresh" {
    assert seal_verdict(1, "specs/a/x.t27", "specs/a/x.t27", "", H_A, 3, 3, 0, 0, 0, 0) == SV_UNKNOWN;
    assert seal_verdict(1, "specs/a/x.t27", "specs/a/x.t27", H_A, "", 3, 3, 0, 0, 0, 0) == SV_UNKNOWN;
    assert seal_verdict(1, "specs/a/x.t27", "specs/a/x.t27", "md5:66cc87ba315b75ba80b51b6813d84cb238149e6e75a4f1f55a5fec4915be7c1f", H_A, 3, 3, 0, 0, 0, 0) == SV_UNKNOWN;
    assert is_fresh("", "") == 0;
}

test "a forced seal is forced, a failing seal is failing" {
    assert seal_verdict(1, "specs/a/x.t27", "specs/a/x.t27", H_A, H_A, 3, 3, 0, 0, 0, 1) == SV_FORCED;
    assert seal_verdict(1, "specs/a/x.t27", "specs/a/x.t27", H_A, H_A, 3, 2, 1, 0, 0, 0) == SV_FAILING;
    assert seal_verdict(1, "specs/a/x.t27", "specs/a/x.t27", H_A, H_A, 3, 3, 0, 1, 0, 0) == SV_FAILING;
    assert seal_verdict(1, "specs/a/x.t27", "specs/a/x.t27", H_A, H_A, 3, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0) == SV_FAILING;
}

test "a green seal with no test, or with a test that asserts nothing, is vacuous" {
    assert seal_verdict(1, "specs/a/x.t27", "specs/a/x.t27", H_A, H_A, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0) == SV_VACUOUS;
    assert seal_verdict(1, "specs/a/x.t27", "specs/a/x.t27", H_A, H_A, 3, 3, 0, 0, 1, 0) == SV_VACUOUS;
}

test "the order: failing outranks vacuous, forced outranks failing" {
    assert seal_verdict(1, "specs/a/x.t27", "specs/a/x.t27", H_A, H_A, 3, 2, 1, 0, 2, 0) == SV_FAILING;
    assert seal_verdict(1, "specs/a/x.t27", "specs/a/x.t27", H_A, H_A, 3, 2, 1, 0, 0, 1) == SV_FORCED;
}

test "the word table agrees with the codes" {
    assert VERDICT_NAME[SV_UNSEALED] == "unsealed";
    assert VERDICT_NAME[SV_STALE] == "stale";
    assert VERDICT_NAME[SV_VERIFIED] == "verified";
    assert str_len(VERDICT_NOTE[SV_VERIFIED]) > 0;
    assert hash_alg(H_A) == ALG_SHA256;
    assert hash_alg("sha256:") == 0;
}

invariant only_verified_is_a_pass {
    assert SV_VERIFIED == 7;
    assert SV_UNSEALED < SV_VERIFIED;
}
